section_1.title: The Hook: The Race of Gravity
section_1.content: Introduce the challenge: A bead slides down a wire from point A to point B under gravity. We compare three paths: a straight line, a circular arc, and a curve. Ask students to intuit which shape wins the race.
section_1.example: Visual: A split-screen animation showing three beads racing; the 'straight line' beads finish slower than the one on the mysterious curved path.

section_2.title: Prerequisite Concept: Conservation of Energy
section_2.content: Briefly review the Work-Energy Theorem. Explain that gravitational potential energy is converted into kinetic energy (v = sqrt(2gh)). The path determines the speed profile at every point.
section_2.example: Visual: A schematic showing a ball at height h gaining velocity as it descends, emphasizing that 'dropping' early increases speed for later stages.

section_3.title: Defining the Brachistochrone
section_3.content: Define 'Brachistochrone' (Greek: shortest time). Explain that the path is not the shortest distance (straight line), but the one that maximizes velocity early on by dipping lower.
section_3.example: Visual: A plot showing how the straight line is too slow initially, while the cycloid path drops steeply to gain velocity before leveling out.

section_4.title: The Mathematical Solution: The Cycloid
section_4.content: Introduce the Cycloid—the path traced by a point on the rim of a rolling circle. Present the parametric equations x = r(θ - sinθ) and y = r(1 - cosθ). Connect this geometry to the physical optimization.
section_4.example: Visual: An animation of a red circle rolling along a ceiling, with a single point tracing out the path (the cycloid) between point A and B.

section_5.title: Real-World Application & Conclusion
section_5.content: Summarize that the shortest time is achieved by a curve that balances distance and velocity. Mention its occurrence in nature, such as a hawk diving for prey at an optimal angle.
section_5.example: Visual: A video clip of a falcon in a 'stoop' (high-speed dive), visually overlaying a cycloid curve to show how nature optimizes the path for the fastest descent.

        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)

        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text("- " + line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # The right side is roughly from x=1.5 to x=6.5
                x = 1.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.0 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines_text = [
            "Which path minimizes the time between these points?",
            "Gravity pulls objects down a wire path.",
            "Compare three paths: straight, arc, and curve.",
            "Which bead reaches the end first?",
            "The answer is not a straight line."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Hook: The Race of Gravity", lecture_lines_text)
        
        # Define paths
        start = self.grid["B1"]
        end = self.grid["E6"]
        
        straight_path = Line(start, end, color=WHITE)
        arc_path = ArcBetweenPoints(start, end, angle=-TAU/8, color=WHITE)
        curve_path = CubicBezier(
            start, 
            start + np.array([1, 1, 0]), 
            end + np.array([-1, 1, 0]), 
            end, 
            color=WHITE
        )
        
        bead1 = Dot(start, color="#FFD700")
        bead2 = Dot(start, color="#FFD700")
        bead3 = Dot(start, color="#FFD700")
        
        self.add(straight_path, arc_path, curve_path, bead1, bead2, bead3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        # Show gravity concept
        gravity_arrow = Arrow(UP, DOWN, color=WHITE).scale(0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(gravity_arrow, "C1")
        self.play(Create(gravity_arrow))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(FadeIn(straight_path), FadeIn(arc_path), FadeIn(curve_path))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        # Racing beads
        self.play(
            MoveAlongPath(bead1, straight_path, run_time=3, rate_func=linear),
            MoveAlongPath(bead2, arc_path, run_time=2.5, rate_func=linear),
            MoveAlongPath(bead3, curve_path, run_time=1.5, rate_func=linear)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FF6347"))
        self.play(Indicate(curve_path, color="#00FFFF"))
        self.wait(2)
